limitations: One local microbenchmark, not full-application/full-Buffer/uniform/statistical-significance proof.
Same exact Weval engine, generic read-only cache, v2 splicer, tools and libcrypto in both arms. JavaScript arm additionally bundles actual Jco1.40/unenv2.0.0-rc.24 Buffer adapter.
Profile enabled in both arms; size difference measures incremental adapter overhead, not minimal profile-off deployment savings.
Ordinary-v5 versus Weval pipelines/static-library and separately built libcrypto bytes differ; these results are not a one-variable Weval causal comparison.
Seven batches within each instance are correlated. Fresh instances share one deserialized component per measurement process; rounds use separate processes.
Compilation is a separate phase; host Instant times operation batches plus the same O(1) visible-result fingerprint. UTF8 inputs are ASCII; string fingerprinting can materialize ropes.
RSS is whole-process high-water including runtime/code/allocator retention; later instance peaks are cumulative within that process.
Largest linear-memory request is a ResourceLimiter maximum desired size for one memory, not live heap, sum of memories, pages committed, allocation count or a leak proof.
No guest clocks/capabilities, DEBUG, fault simulation, raw memory, private introspection or host modification. Local background load and scheduling remain possible confounders.
